mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen each of the last two weeks (-19.9 to -9.0), signaling renewed commuting routines that generate incidental retail and recreation trips, which will keep RETAIL_REC on an upward trajectory over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -19.9 to -9.0 over two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is not higher than its last-28-day mean despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, rejecting the always-on commute-linkage mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has been recovering from -42.0 to -32.7; once TRANSIT crosses above -35 for two consecutive weeks, it indicates a meaningful restoration of public transit use that enables discretionary shopping and leisure trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -35 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of TRANSIT sustaining above -35, indicating transit recovery does not translate into retail footfall.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT produces a compounding effect: commuters returning to offices via transit generate both commute-adjacent and transit-hub retail visits, so their joint improvement predicts a larger RETAIL_REC increase than either series alone over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve week-over-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved concurrently from t-2w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's gain is no larger when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together than when only one rises, rejecting the synergy assumption.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening policy regime, a sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 7.4 to 4.0 over three weeks) signals relaxed stay-at-home requirements, which frees time for out-of-home retail and recreation activity, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise even as RESIDENTIAL continues to decline, or RESIDENTIAL decline coincides with a RETAIL_REC decrease, invalidating the policy-relaxation linkage.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded from -18.6 to -15.6 over the last two weeks, consistent with early seasonal/weather-driven outdoor activity; when PARKS week-over-week increase exceeds 4 points, it indicates a seasonal activity surge that spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 4 points week-over-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase in the week following a PARKS jump exceeding 4 points, indicating no seasonal spillover effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility is stabilizing near baseline (-5.4 to -1.9), suggesting essential-trip demand is saturating; once GROCERY_PHARM week-over-week change stays within ±2 points for two consecutive weeks, further essential-trip gains will not drive additional discretionary retail growth, causing RETAIL_REC to flatten or decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM week-over-week change stays within +/-2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved only from -3.9 to -1.9 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise despite GROCERY_PHARM plateauing within +/-2 points, rejecting the saturation hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL time-at-home and an increase in PARKS activity indicates households substituting outdoor leisure for in-home time; this combined behavioral shift drives bundled outdoor-plus-retail trips (e.g., dining, shopping after park visits), raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks more than either series predicts alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls and PARKS rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell while PARKS rose from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls and PARKS rises jointly, indicating no behavioral substitution effect into retail.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvements decelerate to less than 2 points week-over-week, the metro area has entered a steady-state post-recovery regime where marginal commute-driven retail demand saturates, causing RETAIL_REC growth to stall or reverse over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT week-over-week changes both fall below 2 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held flat at -9.0 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC keeps rising even after WORKPLACES and TRANSIT growth decelerates below 2 points, rejecting the saturation/steady-state mechanism.
